rules.title: Maximum tenant screening fee for 2026
rules.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee a landlord may charge for 2026 is $68.96. The page attributes the limit to California Civil Code Section 1950.6.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96
rules.interaction: Berkeley BMC 13.78.010 requires owners to disclose this state fee cap to applicants.

rules.title: No screening fee when no rental unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Return screening fee to unselected applicants unless first-qualified policy applies
rules.requirement: A landlord must return the screening fee to any applicant not selected. Alternatively, the landlord may have a policy under which it reviews applications in the order received, the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and no screening fee is charged to any applicant not considered.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they: (1) review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and (2) do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.

rules.title: Landlord must use a tenant-provided reusable screening report
rules.requirement: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee rights statement and fee cap disclosure
rules.requirement: When an owner or the owner's agent receives a request to rent residential property in Berkeley and charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must give the applicant a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Civil Code 1950.6(b). The owner may give these in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee. The statement may be the quoted text or a substantially similar one.
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.interaction: BMC 13.78.018 states that Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language. The rights statement refers to a URL the City has not yet provided.

rules.title: No non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants
rules.requirement: An owner of residential rental property, or the owner's agent, cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part. This includes any fee tied to a roommate's departure or to a request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part
rules.interaction: BMC 13.78.018 states that Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language. Lease provisions that violate the chapter are unenforceable.
